OpenCut v1: a standalone headless video editor

Build: cargo build --no-default-features --features cli --bin opencut
Run opencut --help or opencut <command> --help for exact flags.
Use --json on any command. stdout contains results; stderr contains progress.
Render progress updates at most once every five seconds, plus a final completion
update after the file is saved. Use --progress none for silent rendering.

Workflow:
  opencut new project.timeline.json --fps 30000/1001 --json
  opencut probe media.mp4 --json
  opencut edit project.timeline.json add-clip --track TRACK_ID --asset media.mp4 --at 0 --in 1s --out 3s --json
  opencut validate project.timeline.json --json
  opencut inspect project.timeline.json --json
  opencut still project.timeline.json --at 50% -o preview.png
  opencut render project.timeline.json -o output.mp4 --dry-run --json
  opencut render project.timeline.json -o output.mp4 --progress json --json
  opencut schema

Document API: opencut schema emits the authoritative JSON Schema.
Required root fields: version:1, settings, assets, tracks, clips.
Assets: {id,path}; relative paths resolve from the document directory.
Tracks: {id,kind:"video"|"audio"|"text",name,muted}. Later tracks render on top.
Clips: type:"media"|"image"|"text", id, track_id, timeline_start.
Media: asset_id, source_in, source_out. Image: asset_id,length. Text: length,properties.
Frame positions and lengths are integers at settings.frame_rate {numerator,denominator}.
Text length additionally accepts {secs,nanos}. All intervals are end-exclusive.
CLI times: 12.5, 12.5s, 375f, 00:00:12.500; rounded to nearest frame.
Only still --at accepts percentages, with 100% selecting the last frame.
Positions are normalized center anchors, 0..1. Scale 1 fits inside the frame.
Text color is packed RRGGBBAA; background and dip color are #RRGGBB[AA].
Effects apply in order: gaussian_blur(radius pixels), color_adjust(brightness -1..1,
contrast/saturation 0..10), crop(normalized x,y,width,height), flip(horizontal,vertical).
Opacity is a clip property. All effects are static.
Transitions: id,type,from_clip,to_clip,duration; types crossfade,dip_to_color,wipe,slide.
Wipe/slide direction: left,right,up,down. Dip requires color.
Transitions center on adjacent cuts, need source handles, preserve total duration,
and cannot have overlapping windows. Incoming audio uses sin, outgoing cos.
Audio is mixed to stereo, clipped to [-1,1], without a limiter. Compositing uses
8-bit sRGB RGBA; output is BT.709. HDR and keyframe animation are unsupported.

Edit commands: add-track,add-clip,add-text,move-clip,trim-clip,split-clip,remove-clip,set.
IDs are strings, generated as ULIDs; references never use array indexes.
Split --at is an absolute timeline time. Edits return affected entities with IDs.
Set accepts dotted static property paths and JSON values; identities/timing use
dedicated commands. Unknown fields survive edits; invalid edits do not write.
Image add-clip defaults to 5s; --out sets image duration and --in must be zero.
New refuses existing files. Render/still require --overwrite for existing outputs.
Render embeds the input document in metadata unless --no-metadata is given.
Render --bitrate (alias --video-bitrate) accepts bits/s, e.g. 1500000, 1500k, 1.5M.
Absent --bitrate, use the source video bitrate, duration-weighted across contributing
video clips in the selected range. Fall back to the preset only without known source
bitrates. Dry-run reports video_bitrate and bitrate_source. ProRes is profile-controlled.
Exit codes: 0 success, 2 usage, 3 validation, 4 media, 5 rendering, 6 I/O.
JSON errors: {error:{code,pointer,message,file,line}}. Validation returns findings.
This format is independent of the GUI editor format.
